sampling_model.design: Observational two-period binary panel with exact inversion of the sixteen-cell law.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent units drawn from the population law \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: The binary predetermined covariate \(X_t\) is not randomized. Initial assignment and the feedback distribution of \(X_2\) after \((X_1,Y_1)\) may depend arbitrarily on \(u\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell is positive. The weak latent model permits zero assignment or feedback probabilities; the strict latent model requires almost-everywhere positivity, with no numerical lower bound. Observed-cell positivity alone does not imply the strict latent condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cell law is estimated by multinomial frequencies. Whole-set inversion uses simultaneous Clopper--Pearson marginal intervals, while fixed-slope endpoint estimation projects frequencies onto the relevant attainable affine hull.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 1 gives the sharp two-period unrestricted-feedback program conditional on \(X_1\) for a maintained heterogeneity support and reference measure; Sections 5.1--5.3 use density representations and support grids for continuous-support computation.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:exact-feedback-cone-all-laws gives the present all-laws finite certificate; thm:exact-feedback-cone and lem:bdg-continuous-feedback-program prove the positive-margin unrestricted-measure translation. The strict fiber is additional, and no density-subclass equality is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 characterizes the identified set by conditional moment equalities with generalized moments in a truncated Stieltjes cone.
Theorem 1 characterizes all feedback and heterogeneity robust moment conditions for the common parameter.
The main theorem replaces a latent distribution by a finite-dimensional identification-equivalent distribution for discrete covariates.
The paper constructs root-\(n\) outer bounds and asymptotically valid confidence intervals for average-effect identified sets.

body.tldr: For the two-period binary logit panel with a predetermined binary covariate, unrestricted feedback, and an arbitrary heterogeneity law on \(0,\infty\), the independently defined weak and strict joint slope--APE fibers equal finite quartic Stieltjes feasibility sets for every observed probability vector, including zero-cell laws. Eight coupled response-type measures reconstruct one legal history-conditioned sequential model without cross-world independence. The weak lift has fifty-six variables with eight \(3\times3\) and eight augmented \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; the strict lift has sixty-four variables and eight additional \(6\times6\) common-range blocks. Universally, \(\operatorname{sign}(\Delta)=\operatorname{sign}(\theta)\) for nonzero \(\theta\) and \(|\Delta|\le\tanh(|\theta|/4)\), with equality exactly at \(\mu=\delta_{e^{-\theta/2}}\). This envelope is only an outer containment at fixed \(P\), though sharp across varying admissible laws. Fixed-slope endpoint values have separate attainment tests; no fixed-\(P\) attainment is automatic. Algebraic inputs admit terminating exact membership and projection, multinomial inversion gives whole-set coverage, and endpoint consistency is proved only at fixed-slope relative-interior attainable laws.

project_justification.gap: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham give a sharp two-period unrestricted-feedback program conditional on \(X_1\) for a maintained support and reference measure, and their continuous-support computations use densities and support grids. They do not give the present all-laws finite joint-response Stieltjes certificate or its reverse reconstruction from one unconditional mixing law. The published comparator also does not supply the sharp sign-sensitive envelope \(|\Delta|\le\tanh(|\theta|/4)\).
project_justification.niche: A product coupling of the two feedback-coordinate marginals creates eight response types as a construction, without imposing cross-world independence. Their binary-logit path likelihoods share one positive quartic denominator, leaving five bounded moments per type. Separate open-half-line representability yields the weak cone, while common Hankel range is the exact extra certificate used to obtain one positive node set with every type weight positive for the strict class.
project_justification.fill: The note proves forward and reverse maps between the independently defined sequential legal models and finite Stieltjes lifts on the entire observed-law simplex. The main theorem covers zero cells and singular moment faces. Positive cells are used in the comparison corollary only to guarantee \(q_x>0\), after which normalization of \(h_xd\mu\) and the reverse Radon--Nikodym mixture recover the Bonhomme--Dano--Graham unrestricted-measure fiber. The strict class is additional, and no equality with a separately imposed Lebesgue-density subclass is claimed. The sharp universal envelope, exact endpoint values with separate inclusion flags, algebraic decision, whole-set coverage, and fixed-slope relative-interior consistency are downstream consequences.

body.related_work: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Proposition 1, characterize the sharp two-period unrestricted-feedback model conditional on \(X_1\) for a maintained heterogeneity support and reference measure; Sections 5.1--5.3 implement continuous-support calculations with density representations and support grids. After adjoining positive margins, the present weak unrestricted-measure model is equivalent through \(\pi_x(E)=q_x^{-1}\int_Eh_xd\mu\) and the reverse formulas \(\mu=\sum_xq_x\pi_x\), \(h_x=d(q_x\pi_x)/d\mu\). This proved translation permits atomic, absolutely continuous, and mixed probability laws on \(0,\infty\); it does not establish equality with a separately imposed Lebesgue-density subclass. The strict initial-and-feedback-positive fiber is an additional subclass. Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026) supply truncated-Stieltjes tools for a different conditional structure, not reconstruction of the separately unknown feedback kernel here. Curto--Fialkow and Bayer--Teichmann supply classical moment and cubature substrate. The Arellano--Carrasco predetermined-children labor-participation design is the intended empirical consumer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The strict common-support proof is existential and does not provide a certified efficient atom-extraction algorithm. Real quantifier elimination terminates for algebraic inputs but has no asserted polynomial complexity or numerical-stability guarantee. A closed lifted PSD set can have a nonclosed projection, so no fixed-law endpoint-attainment claim is made. Relative-interior convex continuity is pointwise at fixed \(c\); it supplies neither continuity on attainable boundary faces nor uniform inference across Hankel-rank changes or the observable-map rank loss at \(c=1\).
body.honest_scope: The proved contribution is the exact finite-certificate equivalence for the independently defined two-period binary weak and strict fibers on all observed probability laws. Its ingredients are the forward joint-response construction, reverse Radon--Nikodym legal-kernel reconstruction under the history-conditioned sequential response restriction, and the common-support certificate required for strict positivity. Heterogeneity is an arbitrary probability law on the continuous state space \(0,\infty\), not necessarily a density. Positive margins are needed only for the conditional-on-\(X_1\) comparator translation; the strict fiber is additional, and no absolutely-continuous replacement theorem is proved. The universal sign-sensitive slope--APE envelope is sharp across laws but only an outer containment for fixed \(P\). Fixed-slope endpoint values are sharp, while their attainment remains subject to separate tests. The note also proves algebraic membership and projection, conservative exact multinomial whole-set inversion, and endpoint consistency only for fixed \(c\) at relative-interior attainable laws. Continuity at relative-boundary laws, uniform inference on rank-changing faces, and joint consistency as \(c\) approaches one remain open, as do certified extraction, arbitrary \(T\), restricted feedback dynamics, and multinomial outcomes.
body.interpretation: The finite cone is an observed-law identifying map for an independently defined causal slope--APE set, not a regression estimand, discretization, or outer approximation. Its equality is sharp for every observed probability vector. In contrast, the analytic inequality \(|\Delta|\le\tanh(|\theta|/4)\) is an outer envelope for a fixed observed law and is sharp only across varying admissible laws; equality at nonzero slope requires \(\mu\) to concentrate at \(u=c^{-1/2}\). Exact fixed-slope infima and suprema need not belong to the fixed-\(P\) fiber, so lower and upper inclusion are tested separately. Weak feasibility allows different type supports; strict feasibility uses common Hankel range to produce one positive-node support with every type weight positive and hence strictly positive reconstructed initial and feedback kernels almost everywhere.
